title: Where is the other hole in each shape?
description: Five shapes each show one hole and a dashed line. Each hole has a partner on the other side of the line, at the same distance from it.
teaching_notes: One idea: a hole and its partner are mirror pictures, so they sit at the same distance from the line of symmetry, on opposite sides. Watch for students who place the partner on the same side of the line.

video_script.why: The child finds the partner of a hole by reflecting it in the dashed line: a right angle to the line, then the same distance on the other side.
video_script.substitution: Treat the dashed line as a crease: the hole prints its partner on the other side, at the same distance from the line.
video_script.anchor: five shapes, each with one hole and a dashed line: a square with a slanting line, a square with a flat middle line, a triangle with an upright line, and two circles with slanting lines
video_script.payoff_line: The other hole is the mirror picture of the given hole in the dashed line

final_answer.value: In every shape, the other hole is the mirror image of the given hole in the dashed line: the same distance from the line, on the opposite side
final_answer.spoken: the other hole sits at the same distance from the dashed line, on the opposite side

names.{{NAME_4}}: activity: punch holes in folded paper to create symmetric patterns

hold_back: mirror picture of the given hole
maths_rules: A hole and its partner are mirror images in the line of symmetry
The line joining a hole to its partner meets the line of symmetry at a right angle
The hole and its partner are at the same distance from the line, on opposite sides
Square, horizontal middle line, hole in the lower right: the other hole is directly above it, in the upper right
Triangle, vertical line through the top corner, hole left of the line: the other hole is right of the line at the same height
Square, diagonal from top left to bottom right, hole near the top left: the other hole is across the diagonal, near the top edge
Circle, slanted diameter, hole above the line near the right: the other hole is below the line, mirrored
Circle, diagonal from top left to bottom right, hole near the top left and close to the line: the other hole is on the other side of the diagonal, mirrored and close to the line
Check: folding along the dashed line puts the given hole on the new hole
video_script.design: One idea: the partner of a hole is its mirror picture in the dashed line. Assumes the child knows a fold makes a mirror picture. Wrong idea: the partner is on the same side of the line. The five shapes stay on the board all video.
